newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican judge frees seven Zapatista rebels.
newsitem.headline: Mexican judge frees seven Zapatista rebels.

text.p: A Mexican judge on Friday freed seven alleged Zapatista rebels whose arrest in February 1995 on terrorism charges triggered a full-scale manhunt for their leader Subcommander Marcos.

The rebels's political wing, the Zapatista National Liberation Front, said the seven would be let out of a Mexico City jail after being cleared of a roster of charges that included rebellion, terrorism, firearms possession, the manufacture of bombs and storage of explosive materials.

They were arrested in February 1995 preparing what President Ernesto Zedillo had said was a bombing and terrorist campaign that threatened to take the Zapatista conflict beyond the southeastern state of Chiapas.

He used the discovery of arms caches in Mexico City and the eastern state of Veracruz to explain the launch of a massive manhunt for Marcos, who has led the rebels since they started the rebellion for democracy and Indian rights in January 1994.

After arresting the Zapatista suspects, Zedillo revealed the name of the masked rebel subcommander, who until then had kept his identify a well-guarded secret. Despite sending 2,000 troops to Chiapas, Zedillo failed to catch him.
Recently, there have been signs of a thawing between the two adversaries. In December, they swapped letters in an unusual bid to shore up troubled peace efforts.
